confirmed: All six outcomes are scored on each participant's one submitted solution by two raters, not self-reported: 'Two trained experts independently scored all (100%) of the 196 scripts blind to experimental condition.' Each solution got 1-7 originality, usefulness, and elaboration scores under the Consensual Assessment Technique (p. 15, Scoring Procedure; p. 16, first paragraph). The self-assessed originality and usefulness ratings are separate exploratory measures, and the form correctly leaves them out (p. 10; p. 12; p. 18, Results; p. 27).

Construct codes follow the paper's definitions and codebook section 6. 'Originality refers to the uniqueness of an idea' gives novelty. Usefulness is how well an idea fulfils the task goals, which gives usefulness. 'Elaboration refers to how detailed an idea is' gives elaboration. No outcome compares people with each other, so no diversity or flexibility code applies (p. 15, Intervention and Post-Intervention Creative Tasks).

measure expert_raters holds. The paper calls the raters 'trained experts' who were 'well-experienced in scoring diverse creative tasks', and later 'the expert raters'. They are not lay or crowd raters (p. 15, Scoring Procedure; p. 16, first paragraph; p. 27, Self-Assessment of Creative Task Performance).

S1-O1 to S1-O3 were produced with ChatGPT available to both AI arms. The paper says the first task was completed 'with ChatGPT assistance in both AI groups' (p. 9, Design) and that 'both AI groups had a separate window open with ChatGPT-4 during the intervention' (p. 13, Procedure; also p. 14, Intervention Stage). So ai_available_when_produced 'yes' and question with_ai follow the codebook rule for constructs other than diversity.

One point is soft, and the form already records it in S1-O1's measure_detail and in open_questions. The regulated-AI arm wrote its scored idea in Phase 3, which p. 14 describes as 'independently refine and submit'. Fig. 1 labels it 'Phase 3: Independently refine best idea (3 min)', and the same flowchart glosses the human-only arm as 'Solve task independently without ChatGPT assistance' (p. 13). The paper never says the ChatGPT window was closed in Phase 3. Phase 3 also builds on the Phase 2 ChatGPT notes ('Based on your initial ideas and interaction with ChatGPT', p. 35, Appendix A). So with_ai remains the better reading.

S1-O4 to S1-O6 were produced after AI was removed for everyone: 'All participants solved this task independently (i.e., without any access to ChatGPT or the sample prompts that had been presented to the regulated-AI group during the intervention)' (p. 14, Post-Intervention Stage). So ai_available_when_produced 'no' and question after_ai follow the codebook rule.

Timing 'immediate' holds for S1-O4 to S1-O6. The product invention task came in the same session, right after the post-intervention questionnaire, and the whole session lasted about 30 min. The paper gives no gap in minutes, as the delay text says (p. 11, Post-Intervention Creative Task; p. 13, Procedure and Fig. 1).

Unit 'participant' is the paper's own. The two experts' mean ratings 'were then used in subsequent analyses' (p. 16). The tests are 3 x 2 mixed ANOVAs with F(2, 193), which fits 196 participants (pp. 20 and 22). I recomputed d from the printed arm means and SDs with arm sizes 64, 67, and 65 (p. 8, Design; Table 4, p. 20). This reproduces all 18 printed d values within rounding, which shows the SDs are at the participant level.

All 18 'reported' strings match the PDF exactly: arm means and SDs, Bonferroni p-values, and d. The sources are originality (p. 20), usefulness (pp. 20 and 22), and elaboration (p. 22). This includes the negative d printed for regulated-AI against general-AI on the first task (-0.62 and -0.60), although the sentence names general-AI first. The Fig. 2 bars agree (p. 21).

The '(Bonferroni)' label is stated on p. 20 for the originality and usefulness contrasts. The elaboration subsection does not restate it (p. 22), but the elaboration p-values are still corrected values. Uncorrected p for the printed d = 0.11 and 0.13 at these group sizes is about .51 and .46, so a printed p = 1.00 can only be a capped Bonferroni value (p. 22, Elaboration in Creative Tasks).

Directions match the printed p-values and signs in all 18 contrasts. Comparison types follow codebook section 5: ai_vs_bau against human-only, and ai_design with the proposed regulated-AI configuration as treatment and plain general-AI use as control (pp. 20-22; p. 7, The Present Study).

The numbers in measure_detail match the PDF. Interaction F(2, 193) = 13.80, 11.08, and 21.82 (pp. 20 and 22). ICCs are .958, .968, and .991, and .965, .953, and .984, each with its CI (p. 16). The indirect effects are 0.61 [0.12, 1.19] and 0.13 [-0.27, 0.62] (p. 26, Fig. 3).

primary 'paper_primary' holds for all six. The paper names the originality and usefulness of solutions on both tasks, and their elaboration, as 'primary outcomes' of 'the main confirmatory analyses' (p. 18, Results).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. A full-text search finds no similarity or diversity measure across participants, so no across_people record exists. The AUT fluency and flexibility scores were taken at baseline, before the intervention and without AI (p. 9; p. 13; p. 19, Table 3). Self-assessed creativity is self-report (pp. 10, 12, 27). Prompt-type counts and their correlations describe the ChatGPT transcripts, not rated creativity (pp. 16-18, 22-26).
summary: Every outcome in the c130 form is two blind experts' rating of each participant's single solution, and the question, construct, measure, unit, AI availability, and all 18 reported contrasts match the PDF (pp. 9, 13-16, 18, 20-22). The one soft point is one the form already records: the regulated-AI arm wrote its scored product-improvement idea in a Phase 3 that the paper calls independent, but the paper also says both AI groups had ChatGPT-4 open during the intervention, so with_ai stands.
